title: "Reconstruction at arbitrary mortality levels"
subtitle: "The typical schedule plus a regime's deviation, chosen by a hold-out over populations"

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Paper correspondence
Paper §5 ("Schedules at Any Level of Mortality"): the forward model and its inverse
(§5.1), the trajectories (§5.2), the hold-out that measures how well the schedules are
rebuilt (§5.3), and the trajectories of the regimes, their properties and their limits
(§5.4).  Produces the tables `tbl-s6-recon-accuracy` and `tbl-s6-recon-verification` and the
figures `fig-s6-example-schedules`, `fig-s6-age-rotation`, `fig-s6-recon-accuracy`,
`fig-s6-trajectory-scatter`, `fig-s6-cluster-vs-global` and `fig-s6-sex-diff-trajectory`, all
in the companion only.  Also produces the in-text numbers with prefix `traj`, and the
artefact `trajectories` that later chapters use
to generate a schedule for any regime at any e₀.  Parameters:
`config/params.d/trajectories.toml`.  Code: `mdmx.trajectories`.
:::

```{python}
#| label: c07-setup
#| code-summary: "Chapter setup"
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

from mdmx import artifacts, latex, lifetable, plotting, provenance
from mdmx import clustering as clus
from mdmx import nn as mnn
from mdmx import svdcomp as sc
from mdmx import trajectories as tr
from mdmx.config import params

provenance.start_chapter("07-trajectories")
plotting.use_style()
P = params()
PT = P.section("trajectories")                 # config/params.d/trajectories.toml
PF = P.clustering.section("features")          # the typical schedule's LOWESS settings (chapter 06)

clusters_art = artifacts.load("clustering")
tucker = artifacts.load("tucker")
T = artifacts.load("tensor")
populations = artifacts.load("populations")

c_idx, t_idx = clusters_art["c_idx"], clusters_art["t_idx"]
pops, years = np.asarray(clusters_art["pops"]), np.asarray(clusters_art["years"])
ages = np.asarray(tucker["ages"])
e0 = clusters_art["e0_mean"]                    # (n,) sex-average e0 of the observed schedules
e0_sex = clusters_art["e0"]                     # (n, S)
labels, K = clusters_art["labels"], int(clusters_art["K"])
NOISE = [int(k) for k in clusters_art["noise_clusters"]]
REGIMES = [k for k in range(K) if k not in NOISE]   # the regimes later chapters use
U_sex, U_age = tucker["U_sex"], tucker["U_age"]
G_obs = clus.observed_cores(tucker["G_ct"], c_idx, t_idx)       # (n, r1, r2)
z_obs = np.moveaxis(T["M"][:, :, c_idx, t_idx], -1, 0)           # (n, S, A) observed logit(q_x)
grid = clusters_art["conditional_mean"]["e0_grid"]
fidx = clusters_art["features"]["index"]
family = sc.population_families(pops, populations)[c_idx]
TYPICAL = {"frac": PF["conditional_frac"], "iterations": PF["conditional_iterations"],
           "delta_share": PF["conditional_delta"]}
BRACKET = PT["calibration_bracket"]
CL = list(plotting.CLUSTER_COLORS)
SEXES = plotting.SEX_LABELS
n_obs = len(e0)


# Number words for macro names (LaTeX macro names cannot contain digits), as in chapter 06.
WORDS = ["One", "Two", "Three", "Four", "Five", "Six", "Seven", "Eight", "Nine", "Ten",
         "Eleven", "Twelve", "Thirteen", "Fourteen", "Fifteen"]


def cname(k):
    """Cluster names as in chapter 06 (numbered from 1)."""
    return f"Cluster {k + 1}"
```

## What this chapter does

A model life table system must produce a complete schedule of mortality
at *any* level, including levels not observed in any country-year.  Paper
§5 does this for a regime $k$ and a target life expectancy $x$.  Life
expectancy alone does not determine a schedule — infinitely many
schedules share an e₀ (paper §5.1) — so the regime supplies the shape.

Chapter 06 defines a regime as a **deviation pattern from the typical
schedule at the same e₀**.  The natural generator is therefore

$$
\mathcal{G}_k(x) \;=\; \bar{\mathcal{G}}(x) + \mathbf{D}_k(x),
\qquad
\mathbf{z}_k(x) \;=\; \mathbf{S}\,\mathcal{G}_k(x)\,\mathbf{A}^\top ,
$$

the typical effective core at $x$ — the e₀-conditional mean of chapter 06,
whose schedule is the paper's typical schedule $\bar{\mathcal{M}}(x)$ (Eq. 10) — plus the
regime's deviation, mapped to logit($q_x$) for both sexes (the paper's trajectory of a
regime, Eq. 13 in §5.2).  The chapter
asks how the deviation should depend on $x$, answers by a hold-out over
populations, and then examines what the resulting trajectories show:
the sex differential, the change in the age pattern as e₀ rises, and how
well a schedule's regime and e₀ can be recovered from the schedule.

## Step 1 — the typical schedule and the level calibration

The typical effective core $\bar{\mathcal{G}}(x)$ is chapter 06's
e₀-conditional mean: a LOWESS of every core entry against the e₀ of the
observed schedules (span `{python} f"{PF['conditional_frac']}"`), stored on
a grid of `{python} f"{len(grid)}"` e₀ values from
`{python} f"{grid[0]:.1f}"` to `{python} f"{grid[-1]:.1f}"`.  Its schedule's
e₀ is close to $x$ but not equal to it: the mean of the cores at a given
e₀ is not a core with exactly that e₀, because the life table is not
linear in logit($q_x$).  `mdmx.trajectories.calibrate_level` therefore
shifts the **level coordinate** $\mathcal{G}[1,1]$, which moves logit($q_x$)
up or down at almost every age at once, until the schedule's sex-average
e₀ equals $x$; the coordinates that carry the shape are left alone.  The
shift is found by bisection, and the step stops with an error rather than
returning an uncalibrated schedule if the target cannot be bracketed.

```{python}
#| label: c07-typical
#| code-summary: "The typical schedule: its e0 before and after calibration"
typical_only = tr.build_model(grid, clusters_art["conditional_mean"]["core"],
                              np.zeros((0, len(grid), len(fidx))), np.zeros((0, 2)), [], fidx, U_sex,
                              U_age, "typical")
xs_all = np.arange(np.ceil(grid[0]), grid[-1] + 1e-9, PT["curve_step"])
typ_gap = tr.uncalibrated_e0_gap(typical_only, None, xs_all)
calibrated_e0 = tr.sex_e0(tr.generate(typical_only, None, xs_all, bracket=BRACKET)).mean(axis=-1)
print(f"Typical schedule, e0 = {xs_all[0]:.0f} … {xs_all[-1]:.1f}: e0 before calibration minus target "
      f"from {typ_gap.min():+.2f} to {typ_gap.max():+.2f} years (mean {typ_gap.mean():+.2f}); "
      f"after calibration the largest error is {np.abs(calibrated_e0 - xs_all).max():.1e} years")
latex.report("trajTypicalGapMin", float(typ_gap.min()), digits=2, signed=True,
             desc="Smallest e0 gap of the uncalibrated typical schedule (years)")
latex.report("trajTypicalGapMax", float(typ_gap.max()), digits=2, signed=True,
             desc="Largest e0 gap of the uncalibrated typical schedule (years)")
```

Before calibration the typical schedule's e₀ is between
`{python} f"{typ_gap.min():+.2f}"` and `{python} f"{typ_gap.max():+.2f}"`
years from the target, `{python} "above" if typ_gap.mean() > 0 else "below"`
it on average (`{python} f"{typ_gap.mean():+.2f}"`): a schedule averaged in
logit($q_x$) does not have the average e₀ of the schedules it averages.
After calibration the e₀ is exact.

## Step 2 — the deviation, chosen by a hold-out over populations

How should a regime's deviation depend on the level of mortality?  The
candidates:

* **typical** — no deviation: every regime gets the typical schedule (the
  baseline: the typical schedule of all populations, paper Eq. 10);
* **constant** — the regime's mean deviation at every e₀ (the definition of
  a regime in chapter 06);
* **LOWESS** — a LOWESS of the regime members' features against e₀, so that
  the deviation changes with the level of mortality (a per-regime
  trajectory in level-free form), with span
  `{python} ", ".join(f"{f:g}" for f in PT["lowess_fracs"])` of the
  regime's members;
* **neural** — one small network for all regimes from the regime and e₀ to
  the features (`mdmx.nn`; settings in the parameter file), trained with
  early stopping on whole held-out families.

Each of the last three is tried on chapter 06's feature positions alone
and **with the sex contrast of the level column** added
(`mdmx.trajectories.deviation_positions`).  Chapter 06 builds the regimes
without the level column, so on its features alone a regime keeps its
shape but takes the typical overall sex differential; the sex contrast of
the level column — how far apart male and female mortality sit overall —
lets it keep its own: without it, the female advantage of the Central-Eastern European regime
comes out too small (Step 3 measures by how much).  Adding the sex contrast to chapter 06's
clustering features instead turned the regimes into eras, so it enters
through the deviation.  Outside a regime's central e₀ range (its *support*: the
`{python} f"{100 * PT['support_quantiles'][0]:.0f}"`–`{python} f"{100 * PT['support_quantiles'][1]:.0f}"`
% range of its members) a deviation is held at its value at the boundary.

The candidates are compared on schedules the fits have not seen.  Whole
population families — a population with its HMD parts, because the years
of one population are not independent — are dealt into
`{python} f"{PT['n_folds']}"` folds (`svdcomp.assign_folds`).  For each fold,
the typical schedule and every candidate are estimated from the other
folds; each held-out country-year's schedule is then generated from its
regime at its observed e₀, calibrated to that e₀, and compared with the
observed schedule: the **RMSE of logit($q_x$)** over both sexes and ages
0–109 (`mdmx.trajectories.holdout_scores`).  The rule, fixed before the
run: **the candidate with the lowest pooled held-out RMSE over the
non-noise regimes is used**.  The deviations are estimated from the
non-noise regimes only, as in the model the chapter keeps; the noise
cluster is scored in a separate run (without the neural candidate) for
information.  The regime labels come from chapter 06's clustering of all
data, so the hold-out asks how well a schedule is rebuilt *given* its
regime — as in an application where the user chooses the regime.  The
LOWESS span is the best of its grid on the same folds, which favours the
LOWESS slightly.

```{python}
#| label: c07-holdout
#| code-summary: "The hold-out over population families (cached; a few minutes)"
def cand_name(kind, frac=None, sex=False):
    """Hold-out name of a candidate, e.g. 'lowess 0.8 + sex level'."""
    base = f"lowess {frac:g}" if kind == "lowess" else kind
    return base + (" + sex level" if sex else "")


if sorted(PT["sex_level_options"]) != [False, True]:
    raise ValueError("sex_level_options must be [false, true]: the chapter compares each deviation with and "
                     "without the sex level.")
CANDIDATES = {"typical": {"kind": "typical"}}
for sex in PT["sex_level_options"]:
    CANDIDATES[cand_name("constant", sex=sex)] = {"kind": "constant", "sex_level": sex}
    for f in PT["lowess_fracs"]:
        CANDIDATES[cand_name("lowess", f, sex)] = {"kind": "lowess", "frac": f, "sex_level": sex}
    CANDIDATES[cand_name("neural", sex=sex)] = {"kind": "neural", "sex_level": sex, **PT["neural"]}
folds = sc.assign_folds(family, PT["n_folds"], PT["fold_seed"])
HOLDOUT = {"feature_index": fidx, "grid": grid, "typical": TYPICAL, "U_sex": U_sex, "U_age": U_age,
           "bracket": BRACKET, "support_quantiles": PT["support_quantiles"]}


def _holdout():
    main_runs = tr.holdout_scores(G_obs, z_obs, e0, labels, family, folds, REGIMES, CANDIDATES, **HOLDOUT)
    noise_cands = {n_: s_ for n_, s_ in CANDIDATES.items() if s_["kind"] != "neural"}
    noise_runs = (tr.holdout_scores(G_obs, z_obs, e0, labels, family, folds, NOISE, noise_cands, **HOLDOUT)
                  if NOISE else pd.DataFrame(columns=main_runs.columns))
    return {"main": main_runs, "noise": noise_runs}


holdout = artifacts.stage(
    "trajectories_holdout", _holdout, inputs=["clustering", "tucker", "tensor", "populations"],
    params={"candidates": CANDIDATES, "folds": {"n": PT["n_folds"], "seed": PT["fold_seed"]},
            "typical": TYPICAL, "bracket": BRACKET, "support": PT["support_quantiles"]},
    code=[_holdout, cand_name, tr, clus, sc.assign_folds, sc.population_families, mnn, lifetable],
    desc="Schedules of held-out population families rebuilt from regime and e0, for each candidate deviation")
main = holdout["main"]
pooled = main.groupby("candidate", sort=False)["mse"].mean().pow(0.5)
by_regime = main.pivot_table(index="candidate", columns="regime", values="mse", aggfunc="mean").pow(0.5)
noise_rmse = holdout["noise"].groupby("candidate")["mse"].mean().pow(0.5)
gap_mae = main.groupby("candidate")["e0_gap"].apply(lambda g: g.abs().mean())
BEST = str(pooled.idxmin())
CHOSEN = CANDIDATES[BEST]
SEX = bool(CHOSEN.get("sex_level", False))


def best_of(kind, sex):
    """The best-scoring candidate of a kind (over spans for the LOWESS), with or without the sex level."""
    names_ = [n_ for n_, s_ in CANDIDATES.items() if s_["kind"] == kind and s_.get("sex_level", False) == sex]
    return str(pooled[names_].idxmin())


print(pd.DataFrame({"pooled RMSE": pooled, "|e0 gap| before calibration": gap_mae}).round(4).to_string())
print(f"\nChosen: {BEST}")
```

```{python}
#| label: c07-choice
#| code-summary: "How much the chosen deviation gains, with a bootstrap over families"
mse_wide = main.pivot_table(index="row", columns="candidate", values="mse")
fam_rows = family[mse_wide.index.to_numpy()]
# The chosen candidate against: the typical schedule; the constant and neural deviations with the same
# treatment of the sex level; and itself with the other treatment of the sex level.
counterpart = cand_name(CHOSEN["kind"], CHOSEN.get("frac"), not SEX) if CHOSEN["kind"] != "typical" else None
RIVALS = {"typical": "typical", "constant": best_of("constant", SEX), "neural": best_of("neural", SEX),
          "sexlevel": counterpart}
compare = {key: tr.paired_rmse_difference(mse_wide[BEST].to_numpy(), mse_wide[other].to_numpy(), fam_rows,
                                          n_resamples=PT["bootstrap_resamples"], seed=PT["bootstrap_seed"])
           for key, other in RIVALS.items() if other is not None and other != BEST}
print(pd.DataFrame(compare).T.round(4).to_string())


def pct_gain(other):
    """Percent by which the chosen candidate's pooled RMSE is below another's."""
    return 100 * (pooled[other] - pooled[BEST]) / pooled[other]


latex.report("trajNFolds", PT["n_folds"], desc="Folds of the hold-out over population families")
latex.report("trajNFamilies", int(np.unique(family).size), desc="Population families in the hold-out")
latex.report("trajNScored", int(main["row"].nunique()), desc="Country-years scored in the hold-out (non-noise regimes)")
latex.report("trajRmseTypical", float(pooled["typical"]), digits=3, desc="Held-out RMSE of logit qx, typical schedule only")
for sex, tail in ((False, ""), (True, "Sex")):
    if sex in PT["sex_level_options"]:
        what = " with the sex level" if sex else ""
        latex.report(f"trajRmseConstant{tail}", float(pooled[best_of("constant", sex)]), digits=3,
                     desc=f"Held-out RMSE of logit qx, constant deviation{what}")
        latex.report(f"trajRmseLowess{tail}", float(pooled[best_of("lowess", sex)]), digits=3,
                     desc=f"Held-out RMSE of logit qx, e0-dependent (LOWESS) deviation{what}, best span")
        latex.report(f"trajRmseNeural{tail}", float(pooled[best_of("neural", sex)]), digits=3,
                     desc=f"Held-out RMSE of logit qx, neural deviation{what}")
latex.report("trajRmseChosen", float(pooled[BEST]), digits=3, desc="Held-out RMSE of logit qx, chosen deviation")
if CHOSEN["kind"] == "lowess":
    latex.report("trajLowessSpan", CHOSEN["frac"], digits=1, desc="LOWESS span of the chosen deviation")
latex.report("trajGainVsTypical", pct_gain("typical"), digits=1,
             desc="Percent by which the chosen deviation's held-out RMSE is below the typical schedule's")
latex.report("trajGainVsConstant", pct_gain(RIVALS["constant"]), digits=1,
             desc="Percent by which the chosen deviation's held-out RMSE is below that of the constant deviation "
                  "with the same treatment of the sex level")
for key, word in (("constant", "Constant"), ("neural", "Neural"), ("sexlevel", "SexLevel")):
    if key in compare:
        c_ = compare[key]
        latex.report(f"trajDiff{word}", float(c_["difference"]), digits=4, signed=True,
                     desc=f"Held-out pooled RMSE of the chosen deviation minus that of its {key} rival")
        latex.report(f"trajDiff{word}Low", float(c_["lower"]), digits=4, signed=True,
                     desc=f"Lower end of the 95% family-bootstrap interval of trajDiff{word}")
        latex.report(f"trajDiff{word}High", float(c_["upper"]), digits=4, signed=True,
                     desc=f"Upper end of the 95% family-bootstrap interval of trajDiff{word}")
        latex.report(f"trajFamiliesBetter{word}", 100 * c_["share_better"], digits=0,
                     desc=f"Percent of population families rebuilt better by the chosen deviation than by its {key} rival")
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-s6-recon-accuracy
#| code-summary: "Table: held-out accuracy by candidate and regime"
def label_of(name):
    spec = CANDIDATES[name]
    base = {"typical": "Typical schedule only", "constant": "Constant deviation",
            "neural": "Neural network"}.get(spec["kind"], f"LOWESS in $e_0$, span {spec.get('frac', 0):g}")
    return base + (", with sex level" if spec.get("sex_level") else "")


noise_col = f"{cname(NOISE[0])} (noise)" if NOISE else "Noise"
acc = pd.DataFrame({"Deviation": [label_of(c) for c in CANDIDATES],
                    "All": [pooled[c] for c in CANDIDATES],
                    **{cname(k): [by_regime.loc[c, k] for c in CANDIDATES] for k in REGIMES},
                    noise_col: [noise_rmse.get(c, np.nan) for c in CANDIDATES],
                    r"$|\Delta e_0|$": [gap_mae[c] for c in CANDIDATES]})
acc_tex = acc.copy()
best_row = list(CANDIDATES).index(BEST)
acc_tex.loc[best_row, "Deviation"] = f"{acc_tex.loc[best_row, 'Deviation']} (chosen)"
# The table standard: the regimes under one spanner, the long names of the deviations wrapped.
acc_tex = acc_tex.rename(columns={**{cname(k): f"Regime: {cname(k).removeprefix('Cluster ')}" for k in REGIMES},
                                  noise_col: f"Regime: {noise_col.removeprefix('Cluster ').replace(' (', chr(10) + '(')}"})
latex.save_table(
    acc_tex, "tbl-s6-recon-accuracy",
    "Accuracy of rebuilt schedules on held-out population families: root-mean-square difference "
    "between the generated and the observed $\\operatorname{logit}({}_1q_x)$ (both sexes, ages 0--109), by deviation and "
    f"regime, over {PT['n_folds']} folds of whole families.  Each schedule is generated from its regime "
    "at its observed $e_0$ and calibrated to that $e_0$.  \\emph{With sex level}: the deviation also "
    "shifts the sex contrast of the level column.  \\emph{All}: pooled over the non-noise regimes, "
    "which decides the choice; the noise cluster is scored in a separate run, without the neural "
    "network (--).  $|\\Delta e_0|$: mean absolute difference, before calibration, between the "
    "generated schedule's $e_0$ and the target (years).",
    short_caption="Accuracy of rebuilt schedules (hold-out)", escape_cells=False, spanners=": ",
    wrap={"Deviation": "4.4cm"},
    formats={c: (lambda v: "--" if pd.isna(v) else f"{v:.3f}") for c in acc_tex.columns if c != "Deviation"},
    rank=[latex.Rank([c for c in acc_tex.columns if c not in ("Deviation", r"$|\Delta e_0|$")], "min")],
    rank_note="among the deviations in each RMSE column")
acc.round(4)
```

What the regimes add.  The same hold-out with the typology at
`{python} P.section("checks")["k_alt"]` clusters, the smallest number fitted,
for the chosen deviation and for the typical schedule alone, on the same
country-years (the noise cluster's are left out of both, as above); its settings are in
`config/params.d/checks.toml`.
```{python}
#| label: c07-k-alt
#| code-summary: "The hold-out with the typology at K = 2 (cached)"
CK = P.section("checks")
K_ALT = int(CK["k_alt"])
gmm_fits = artifacts.load("clustering_gmm")["fits"]
if not np.array_equal(gmm_fits[str(K)]["labels"], labels):
    raise ValueError("the stored mixture at the reproducible K does not reproduce the typology's labels: rows differ")
# The noise cluster's country-years are out of the alternative typology too, so both score the same rows.
labels_alt = np.where(np.isin(labels, NOISE), -1, gmm_fits[str(K_ALT)]["labels"])
REGIMES_ALT = sorted(int(k) for k in np.unique(labels_alt) if k >= 0)
CANDS_ALT = {"typical": CANDIDATES["typical"], BEST: CHOSEN}


def _holdout_alt():
    return tr.holdout_scores(G_obs, z_obs, e0, labels_alt, family, folds, REGIMES_ALT, CANDS_ALT, **HOLDOUT)


hold_alt = artifacts.stage(
    f"trajectories_holdout_k{K_ALT}", _holdout_alt,
    inputs=["clustering_gmm", "clustering", "tucker", "tensor", "populations"],
    params={"k_alt": K_ALT, "candidates": CANDS_ALT, "folds": {"n": PT["n_folds"], "seed": PT["fold_seed"]},
            "typical": TYPICAL, "bracket": BRACKET, "support": PT["support_quantiles"]},
    code=[_holdout_alt, tr, clus, sc.assign_folds, sc.population_families, lifetable],
    desc=f"Held-out schedules rebuilt with the typology at K = {K_ALT}")
pooled_alt = hold_alt.groupby("candidate", sort=False)["mse"].mean().pow(0.5)
if abs(pooled_alt["typical"] - pooled["typical"]) > 1e-9:
    raise ValueError("the typical schedule scores differently on the alternative typology's rows")
latex.report("trajKAlt", K_ALT, desc="The alternative number of clusters of the check")
latex.report("trajRmseKAltChosen", pooled_alt[BEST], digits=3,
             desc=f"Pooled held-out RMSE of logit(qx), chosen deviation, typology at K = {K_ALT}")
latex.report("trajGainKAltVsTypical", 100 * (1 - pooled_alt[BEST] / pooled["typical"]), digits=1,
             desc=f"Per cent below the typical schedule alone, typology at K = {K_ALT} (as trajGainVsTypical)")
print(f"Pooled held-out RMSE: typical {pooled['typical']:.4f}; chosen deviation at K = {K} {pooled[BEST]:.4f}, "
      f"at K = {K_ALT} {pooled_alt[BEST]:.4f}")
```

Each held-out country-year above is rebuilt with the regime the clustering gave it, and the
clustering saw that year's own schedule: the gain over the typical schedule is how much the
regimes describe, given the regime.  When the regime is not known it must be guessed without the
schedule.  Here each held-out country-year is given the regime of the nearest country-year of the
other folds in e₀ and calendar year (each standardised by its standard deviation;
`mdmx.trajectories.nearest_regimes`), and the chosen deviation is scored again on the same rows.

```{python}
#| label: c07-blind
#| code-summary: "The hold-out with the regime guessed from e₀ and the year (cached)"
YEAR_ROW = years[t_idx].astype(int)
BLIND = tr.nearest_regimes(e0, YEAR_ROW, labels, folds, REGIMES)
CANDS_BLIND = {BEST: CHOSEN}


def _holdout_blind():
    return tr.holdout_scores(G_obs, z_obs, e0, labels, family, folds, REGIMES, CANDS_BLIND,
                             generate_labels=BLIND, **HOLDOUT)


hold_blind = artifacts.stage(
    "trajectories_holdout_blind", _holdout_blind, inputs=["clustering", "tucker", "tensor", "populations"],
    params={"candidates": CANDS_BLIND, "folds": {"n": PT["n_folds"], "seed": PT["fold_seed"]},
            "typical": TYPICAL, "bracket": BRACKET, "support": PT["support_quantiles"]},
    code=[_holdout_blind, tr, clus, sc.assign_folds, sc.population_families, lifetable],
    desc="Held-out schedules rebuilt with the regime of the nearest country-year of the other folds")
if set(hold_blind["row"]) != set(main.loc[main["candidate"] == BEST, "row"]):
    raise ValueError("the label-blind hold-out scores other rows than the main one")
rmse_blind = float(np.sqrt(hold_blind["mse"].mean()))
scored_rows = hold_blind["row"].to_numpy()
latex.report("trajRmseBlind", rmse_blind, digits=3,
             desc="Pooled held-out RMSE of logit(qx), chosen deviation, regime of the nearest country-year of the "
                  "other folds in e0 and calendar year")
latex.report("trajGainBlindVsTypical", 100 * (1 - rmse_blind / pooled["typical"]), digits=1, signed=True,
             desc="Per cent below the typical schedule alone, with the regime guessed from e0 and the year")
latex.report("trajBlindMatch", 100 * float(np.mean(BLIND[scored_rows] == labels[scored_rows])), digits=0,
             desc="Share (%) of the scored country-years whose guessed regime is the clustering's")
print(f"Regime guessed from e0 and year: pooled RMSE {rmse_blind:.4f} (typical {pooled['typical']:.4f}, "
      f"given the regime {pooled[BEST]:.4f}); guessed regime = the clustering's in "
      f"{100 * np.mean(BLIND[scored_rows] == labels[scored_rows]):.0f} % of the rows")
```

With the regime guessed from e₀ and the year (the clustering's in
`{python} f"{100 * np.mean(BLIND[scored_rows] == labels[scored_rows]):.0f}"` % of the scored
country-years), the chosen deviation's held-out RMSE is `{python} f"{rmse_blind:.3f}"`,
`{python} f"{100 * (1 - rmse_blind / pooled['typical']):.1f}"` % below the typical schedule's
`{python} f"{pooled['typical']:.3f}"` (given the regime: `{python} f"{pct_gain('typical'):.1f}"` %).

## Step 3 — the model

The chosen deviation is estimated once more, on all country-years of the
non-noise regimes, around chapter 06's typical schedule.  The result, the
artefact `trajectories`, holds everything a later chapter needs to
generate a schedule: the e₀ grid, the typical core, each regime's deviation
on the grid, the regimes' supports and the bases (see the end of the
chapter).

```{python}
#| label: c07-model
#| code-summary: "The model on all data (cached artefact `trajectories`)"
def _model():
    positions = tr.deviation_positions(fidx, U_sex.shape[1], sex_level=SEX)
    typical_core = clusters_art["conditional_mean"]["core"]
    # Residuals from the typical schedule's LOWESS values at the data, as in the hold-out (chapter 06's
    # grid curve is that LOWESS interpolated; the two differ by at most 0.02).
    typical_at, _ = clus.conditional_mean(e0, G_obs, grid=grid, **TYPICAL)
    R_all = clus.cores_to_features(G_obs, positions) - clus.cores_to_features(typical_at, positions)
    dev, support = tr.estimate_deviation(R_all, e0, labels, family, REGIMES, grid, CHOSEN,
                                         iterations=PF["conditional_iterations"],
                                         delta_share=PF["conditional_delta"],
                                         support_quantiles=PT["support_quantiles"])
    model = tr.build_model(grid, typical_core, dev, support, REGIMES, positions, U_sex, U_age, CHOSEN["kind"])
    return {**model, "candidate": BEST, "holdout_rmse": pooled.to_frame("rmse").reset_index()}


model = artifacts.stage(
    "trajectories", _model, inputs=["clustering", "tucker", "populations", "trajectories_holdout"],
    params={"chosen": CHOSEN, "support": PT["support_quantiles"], "typical": TYPICAL},
    code=[_model, tr, clus, mnn],
    desc="Typical schedule plus regime deviations: generates a schedule for any regime at any e0")
support = {k: model["support"][i] for i, k in enumerate(REGIMES)}
latex.report("trajSupportLowerPct", 100 * PT["support_quantiles"][0], digits=0,
             desc="Quantile (percent) of the members' e0 at the lower end of a regime's support")
latex.report("trajSupportUpperPct", 100 * PT["support_quantiles"][1], digits=0,
             desc="Quantile (percent) of the members' e0 at the upper end of a regime's support")
for k in REGIMES:
    latex.report(f"trajSupportLow{WORDS[k]}", float(support[k][0]), digits=1,
                 desc=f"Lower end of the e0 support of {cname(k).lower()}")
    latex.report(f"trajSupportHigh{WORDS[k]}", float(support[k][1]), digits=1,
                 desc=f"Upper end of the e0 support of {cname(k).lower()}")
```

For each regime, the generated schedules at its members' own e₀ — before
calibration, how far their e₀ is from the target; after it, their female
and male e₀ — against the members' observed female and male e₀ (both
averaged over the members).  This is an in-sample check: the deviations
were estimated from these members; the out-of-sample evidence is the
hold-out of Step 2.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-s6-recon-verification
#| code-summary: "Table: generated against observed, at each member's own e0"
rows = []
for k in REGIMES:
    m = np.flatnonzero(labels == k)
    e0_fm = tr.sex_e0(tr.generate(model, k, e0[m], bracket=BRACKET))           # (n_k, S)
    gap_k = tr.uncalibrated_e0_gap(model, k, e0[m])
    rows.append({"Cluster": k + 1, "Country-years": int(m.size),
                 r"Support ($e_0$)": f"{support[k][0]:.1f}--{support[k][1]:.1f}",
                 r"Mean $|\Delta e_0|$ before calibration": float(np.abs(gap_k).mean()),
                 r"Female $e_0$": float(e0_fm[:, 0].mean()), r"Male $e_0$": float(e0_fm[:, 1].mean()),
                 r"Observed female $e_0$": float(e0_sex[m, 0].mean()),
                 r"Observed male $e_0$": float(e0_sex[m, 1].mean())})
verify = pd.DataFrame(rows)
verify["gap error"] = ((verify[r"Female $e_0$"] - verify[r"Male $e_0$"])
                       - (verify[r"Observed female $e_0$"] - verify[r"Observed male $e_0$"]))

# The same, for the chosen deviation estimated with the other treatment of the sex level (how much it matters).
other_pos = tr.deviation_positions(fidx, U_sex.shape[1], sex_level=not SEX)
typical_at_data, _ = clus.conditional_mean(e0, G_obs, grid=grid, **TYPICAL)
R_other = clus.cores_to_features(G_obs, other_pos) - clus.cores_to_features(typical_at_data, other_pos)
dev_o, sup_o = tr.estimate_deviation(R_other, e0, labels, family, REGIMES, grid, CHOSEN,
                                     iterations=PF["conditional_iterations"], delta_share=PF["conditional_delta"],
                                     support_quantiles=PT["support_quantiles"])
other_model = tr.build_model(grid, model["typical"], dev_o, sup_o, REGIMES, other_pos, U_sex, U_age, CHOSEN["kind"])
gap_error_other = {}
for k in REGIMES:
    m = np.flatnonzero(labels == k)
    e0_fm = tr.sex_e0(tr.generate(other_model, k, e0[m], bracket=BRACKET))
    gap_error_other[k] = float((e0_fm[:, 0] - e0_fm[:, 1]).mean() - (e0_sex[m, 0] - e0_sex[m, 1]).mean())
print("Sex-gap error (generated − observed, years) with the chosen positions:",
      dict(zip(verify["Cluster"], verify["gap error"].round(2))), "; with the other treatment of the sex level:",
      {k + 1: round(v, 2) for k, v in gap_error_other.items()})
VERIFY_HEAD = {"Cluster": "Regime", "Country-years": "Country-\nyears", r"Support ($e_0$)": "Support\n($e_0$)",
               r"Mean $|\Delta e_0|$ before calibration": "Mean $|\\Delta e_0|$\nbefore calibration",
               "Female $e_0$": "Generated $e_0$: Female", "Male $e_0$": "Generated $e_0$: Male",
               "Observed female $e_0$": "Observed $e_0$: Female", "Observed male $e_0$": "Observed $e_0$: Male"}
verify_tex = verify.drop(columns="gap error").rename(columns=VERIFY_HEAD)
latex.save_table(
    verify_tex, "tbl-s6-recon-verification",
    "The generated schedules of each regime at its members' own $e_0$, against the members' observed "
    "schedules (means over the members).  \\emph{Support}: the "
    f"{100 * PT['support_quantiles'][0]:.0f}--{100 * PT['support_quantiles'][1]:.0f}\\% range of the members' "
    "$e_0$, outside which the deviation is held constant.  $|\\Delta e_0|$: the distance between the $e_0$ "
    "of the uncalibrated schedule (typical core plus deviation) and the target, in years; after "
    "calibration the sex-average $e_0$ equals the target, so the generated and observed female and male "
    "$e_0$ differ only through the sex differential.",
    short_caption="Generated against observed schedules, by regime", escape_cells=False, spanners=": ",
    formats={c: "{:.2f}" for c in verify_tex.columns if c not in ("Regime", "Country-\nyears", "Support\n($e_0$)")})
latex.report("trajVerifyGapMax", float(verify[r"Mean $|\Delta e_0|$ before calibration"].max()), digits=2,
             desc="Largest mean |e0 gap| before calibration of a regime's generated schedules (years)")
latex.report("trajSexGapErrorMax", float(verify["gap error"].abs().max()), digits=2,
             desc="Largest error of a regime's mean generated female-minus-male e0 gap, in-sample (years)")
latex.report("trajSexGapErrorOtherMax", float(max(abs(v) for v in gap_error_other.values())), digits=2,
             desc="The same with the other treatment of the sex level (in-sample, years)")
verify.round(2)
```


## Step 4 — the trajectories

Each curve below is a calibrated generated schedule followed along e₀:
the typical schedule over the whole range, each regime's schedule over its
support.

```{python}
#| label: c07-curves
#| code-summary: "Generated schedules along e0 for the typical schedule and each regime"
def curve_x(lo, hi):
    return np.arange(np.ceil(lo / PT["curve_step"]) * PT["curve_step"], hi + 1e-9, PT["curve_step"])


q_lo, q_hi = np.quantile(e0, PT["curve_quantiles"])
x_typ = curve_x(max(grid[0], q_lo), min(grid[-1], q_hi))
z_typ = tr.generate(model, None, x_typ, bracket=BRACKET)                        # (q, S, A)
x_reg = {k: curve_x(*support[k]) for k in REGIMES}
z_reg = {k: tr.generate(model, k, x_reg[k], bracket=BRACKET) for k in REGIMES}
```

```{python}
    z_lo = tr.generate(model, k, lo_x, bracket=BRACKET)[0] - tr.generate(model, None, lo_x, bracket=BRACKET)[0]
    z_hi = tr.generate(model, k, hi_x, bracket=BRACKET)[0] - tr.generate(model, None, hi_x, bracket=BRACKET)[0]
```

## Step 5 — the sex differential along the trajectories

The female and male schedules are generated together, so the sex
differential along a trajectory comes from the data, not from an
assumption: the typical schedule carries the sex differential observed at
each level of mortality, and `{python} sex_intro`

```{python}
    ax2.plot(x_reg[k], e0_k[:, 0] / e0_k[:, 1], color=CL[k], lw=1.4)

latex.report("trajSexGapMax", float(gap_typ[i_max]), digits=1, desc="Largest female-minus-male e0 gap along the typical schedule (years)")
latex.report("trajSexGapMaxAt", float(x_typ[i_max]), digits=0, desc="Sex-average e0 at which the typical gap is largest")
latex.report("trajSexGapLow", float(gap_typ[0]), digits=1, desc="Typical female-minus-male gap at the low end of the range (years)")
latex.report("trajSexGapHigh", float(gap_typ[-1]), digits=1, desc="Typical female-minus-male gap at the high end of the range (years)")
latex.report("trajSexGapLowAt", float(x_typ[0]), digits=0, desc="Low end of the typical trajectory's range (e0)")
latex.report("trajSexGapHighAt", float(x_typ[-1]), digits=0, desc="High end of the typical trajectory's range (e0)")

# How far each regime's sex gap departs from the typical one at the same e0, over its support.
gap_excess = {}
for k in REGIMES:
    e0_k = tr.sex_e0(z_reg[k])
    typ_at = np.interp(x_reg[k], x_typ, gap_typ)
    gap_excess[k] = float(np.mean(e0_k[:, 0] - e0_k[:, 1] - typ_at))
k_wide, k_narrow = max(gap_excess, key=gap_excess.get), min(gap_excess, key=gap_excess.get)
# The paper words these two as "larger" and "smaller" than the typical gap, so it quotes them unsigned.
if not gap_excess[k_wide] > 0 > gap_excess[k_narrow]:
    raise ValueError(f"The regimes' sex gaps no longer straddle the typical one: {cname(k_wide)} "
                     f"{gap_excess[k_wide]:+.2f}, {cname(k_narrow)} {gap_excess[k_narrow]:+.2f} years.")
print(f"Widest sex gap relative to the typical one: {cname(k_wide)} ({gap_excess[k_wide]:+.2f} y); "
      f"narrowest: {cname(k_narrow)} ({gap_excess[k_narrow]:+.2f} y)")
latex.report("trajSexGapExcessWide", gap_excess[k_wide], digits=1,
             desc=f"Mean excess of {cname(k_wide).lower()}'s female-minus-male e0 gap over the typical one "
                  "at the same e0, over its support (years; the largest)")
latex.report("trajSexGapExcessNarrow", -gap_excess[k_narrow], digits=1,
             desc=f"Mean shortfall of {cname(k_narrow).lower()}'s female-minus-male e0 gap from the typical one "
                  "at the same e0, over its support (years; the largest)")

# The observed gap by band of e0 without the populations whose female advantage is unusually large.
regions = P.clustering.section("regions")
region_of = {p_: r_ for r_, members in regions.items() for p_ in members}
left_out = np.isin([region_of[p_] for p_ in pops[c_idx]], PT["sex_gap_check_regions"])
b_lo, b_hi, b_w = PT["sex_gap_bands"]
band_gap = pd.Series(gap_obs[~left_out]).groupby(pd.cut(e0[~left_out], np.arange(b_lo, b_hi + 1e-9, b_w)),
                                                 observed=True).mean()
i_band = int(np.argmax(band_gap.to_numpy()))
latex.report("trajSexGapCheckLow", float(band_gap.iloc[0]), digits=1,
             desc="Observed female-minus-male gap in the lowest e0 band, without the excluded regions (years)")
latex.report("trajSexGapCheckMax", float(band_gap.iloc[i_band]), digits=1,
             desc="Largest observed band gap without the excluded regions (years)")
latex.report("trajSexGapCheckHigh", float(band_gap.iloc[-1]), digits=1,
             desc="Observed gap in the highest e0 band, without the excluded regions (years)")
print("Observed gap by e0 band without", PT["sex_gap_check_regions"], ":", band_gap.round(1).to_dict())
narrows = gap_typ[-1] < gap_typ[i_max] - PT["sex_gap_narrowing"]
check_narrows = band_gap.iloc[-1] < band_gap.iloc[i_band] - PT["sex_gap_narrowing"] and i_band > 0
sex_text = (f"Along the typical schedule the female advantage is {gap_typ[0]:.1f} years at e₀ = {x_typ[0]:.0f}, "
            f"largest ({gap_typ[i_max]:.1f} years) at e₀ ≈ {x_typ[i_max]:.0f}, and {gap_typ[-1]:.1f} years at "
            f"e₀ = {x_typ[-1]:.0f}" + (": it widens during the mortality transition and narrows again at the "
            "lowest mortality, as the literature documents." if narrows else ".")
            + (f"  This is not merely a matter of which populations are observed at each level: " if check_narrows
               else "  Part of this shape comes from which populations are observed at each level: ")
            + f"without the populations of {' and '.join(PT['sex_gap_check_regions'])}, whose female advantage "
            f"is unusually large, the observed gap is {band_gap.iloc[0]:.1f} years at e₀ "
            f"{band_gap.index[0].left:g}–{band_gap.index[0].right:g}, {band_gap.iloc[i_band]:.1f} at "
            f"{band_gap.index[i_band].left:g}–{band_gap.index[i_band].right:g} and {band_gap.iloc[-1]:.1f} at "
            f"{band_gap.index[-1].left:g}–{band_gap.index[-1].right:g}."
            + f"  The regimes differ here: over its support, {cname(k_wide)}'s female advantage is on average "
            f"{gap_excess[k_wide]:+.1f} years from the typical one at the same e₀, {cname(k_narrow)}'s "
            f"{gap_excess[k_narrow]:+.1f} years.")
sex_text += (f"  At their members' own e₀ the generated female-minus-male gap of every regime is within "
             f"{verify['gap error'].abs().max():.1f} years of the observed one (in-sample; "
             f"{max(abs(v) for v in gap_error_other.values()):.1f} years " + ("without" if SEX else "with")
             + " the sex level).")
if "sexlevel" in compare:
    # Effect of adding the sex level on the held-out RMSE (the comparison is chosen minus its counterpart).
    effect = compare["sexlevel"]["difference"] * (1 if SEX else -1)
    sex_text += (f"  Out of sample, adding the sex level {'lowers' if effect < 0 else 'raises'} the held-out RMSE "
                 f"by {abs(effect):.4f} (Step 2).")
```

`{python} sex_text`

## Step 6 — does the age pattern of decline rotate?

Paper §5.2 motivates the trajectories by the **rotation** of mortality
decline — as e₀ rises, gains shift from young to old ages — and §5.4 measures it.
We examine it
along the typical schedule in two ways
(`mdmx.trajectories.age_contributions`): the slope of logit($q_x$)
per year of e₀ at three levels — the paper's measure — and the **share of a
gain in e₀ that comes from each age group**, from the exact derivative of
e₀ with respect to logit($q_x$) times that slope.  Both use central
differences over ±`{python} f"{PT['rotation_step']:g}"` years of e₀, wide
enough not to follow the small irregularities of the typical schedule
(chapter 06's short smoothing span follows the mix of populations observed
at each level); over such a step the shares are rescaled to add up to one.

```{python}
#| label: c07-rotation
#| code-summary: "Slopes of logit(q_x) and age shares of e0 gains along the typical schedule"
h_rot = PT["rotation_step"]
lev = np.asarray(PT["rotation_e0"], dtype=float)
slope, _ = tr.age_contributions(model, None, lev, bracket=BRACKET, h=h_rot)                  # (L, S, A)
x_rot = curve_x(x_typ[0] + h_rot, x_typ[-1] - h_rot)
_, share_rot = tr.age_contributions(model, None, x_rot, bracket=BRACKET, h=h_rot, normalise=True)  # (q, S, A)
starts = PT["age_groups"]
groups = [(a, b) for a, b in zip(starts, starts[1:] + [len(ages)], strict=True)]
if PT["young_below"] not in starts or PT["old_from"] not in starts:
    raise ValueError("young_below and old_from must be first ages of age groups (age_groups).")
share_grp = np.stack([share_rot[:, :, a:b].sum(axis=(1, 2)) for a, b in groups], axis=1)   # (q, G)
young = share_grp[:, [b <= PT["young_below"] for a, b in groups]].sum(axis=1)
old = share_grp[:, [a >= PT["old_from"] for a, b in groups]].sum(axis=1)
at = [int(np.argmin(np.abs(x_rot - v))) for v in lev]
print(pd.DataFrame(share_grp[at], index=[f"e0 {v:g}" for v in lev], columns=PT["age_group_labels"]).round(3).to_string())
a_hi, a_lo = PT["slope_ratio_ages"]
s_avg = slope.mean(axis=1)                                                               # (L, A) sex average
ratio = s_avg[:, a_hi] / s_avg[:, a_lo]                                                  # (L,)
ad_lo, ad_hi = PT["adult_ages"]
adult = s_avg[:, ad_lo:ad_hi + 1].mean(axis=1) / s_avg[:, a_lo]                          # (L,)
print(f"Slope at age {a_hi} relative to age {a_lo}, by level:", np.round(ratio, 2).tolist())
print(f"Mean slope at ages {ad_lo}–{ad_hi} relative to age {a_lo}, by level:", np.round(adult, 2).tolist())
for i, word in ((0, "Low"), (len(lev) // 2, "Mid"), (len(lev) - 1, "High")):
    v = f"{lev[i]:g}"
    latex.report(f"trajShareYoung{word}", 100 * young[at[i]], digits=0,
                 desc=f"Percent of an e0 gain from ages below {PT['young_below']} at e0 = {v}")
    latex.report(f"trajShareOld{word}", 100 * old[at[i]], digits=0,
                 desc=f"Percent of an e0 gain from ages {PT['old_from']} and over at e0 = {v}")
    latex.report(f"trajSlopeRatio{word}", float(ratio[i]), digits=2,
                 desc=f"Slope of logit qx at age {a_hi} relative to age {a_lo} along the typical schedule at e0 = {v}")
    latex.report(f"trajAdultRatio{word}", float(adult[i]), digits=2,
                 desc=f"Mean slope of logit qx at ages {ad_lo}-{ad_hi} relative to age {a_lo} at e0 = {v}")
    latex.report(f"trajRotation{word}", lev[i], digits=0, desc=f"{word} e0 level of the rotation analysis")
latex.report("trajRotationStep", h_rot, digits=1,
             desc="Half-width (years of e0) of the central differences of the rotation analysis")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-s6-age-rotation
#| fig-cap: "The age pattern of mortality decline along the typical schedule. Left: change of logit(q_x) per year of e₀ (average of the sexes; central differences, step as in the text) at three levels of e₀ — the paper's measure. Right: the share of a gain in e₀ that comes from each age group, by level of e₀ (both sexes)."
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4.2))
shades = plt.cm.Blues(np.linspace(0.45, 1.0, len(lev)))
for i, v in enumerate(lev):
    ax1.plot(ages, slope[i].mean(axis=0), color=shades[i], lw=1.8, label=f"$e_0$ = {v:g}")
ax1.axhline(0, color="black", lw=0.5)
ax1.set_xlabel("Age")
ax1.set_ylabel("d logit$(q_x)$ / d$e_0$")
ax1.legend(fontsize=8)
grp_colors = plt.cm.viridis(np.linspace(0.05, 0.95, len(groups)))
ax2.stackplot(x_rot, share_grp.T, colors=grp_colors, labels=PT["age_group_labels"], edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.4)
ax2.set_xlim(x_rot[0], x_rot[-1])
ax2.set_ylim(0, 1)
ax2.set_xlabel("$e_0$")
ax2.set_ylabel("Share of a gain in $e_0$")
ax2.legend(title="Ages", fontsize=8, loc="center left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.0, 0.5))
fig.tight_layout()
plotting.save_figure(fig, "fig-s6-age-rotation")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: c07-rotation-text
#| output: asis
#| code-summary: "Text: what the rotation analysis shows"
tol = PT["same_shape_tolerance"]
levels_txt = ", ".join(f"{v:g}" for v in lev)


def direction(change):
    """How the age pattern of decline moved between two levels, from the change of a slope ratio."""
    if abs(change) < tol:
        return "hardly changes"
    return "moves towards the young ages" if change < 0 else "moves towards the older ages"


moves = [f"between e₀ = {lev[i]:g} and {lev[i + 1]:g} the decline {direction(adult[i + 1] - adult[i])}"
         for i in range(len(lev) - 1)]
print(f"Measured as the paper does — the slope of logit($q_x$) per year of e₀ — mortality at ages {ad_lo}–{ad_hi} "
      f"falls {', '.join(f'{r:.2f}' for r in adult)} times as fast as at age {a_lo} at e₀ = {levels_txt} "
      f"(at age {a_hi}: {', '.join(f'{r:.2f}' for r in ratio)} times): " + "; ".join(moves) + ".", end="")
rotates = young[at[-1]] < young[at[0]] and old[at[-1]] > old[at[0]]
young_steps = np.diff(young[at])
j_big = int(np.argmin(young_steps))
print(f"  Where the *gains in life expectancy* come from {'does' if rotates else 'does not'} rotate: at "
      f"e₀ = {levels_txt} the shares from ages below {PT['young_below']} are "
      f"{', '.join(f'{100 * young[i]:.0f}' for i in at)}% and from ages {PT['old_from']} and over "
      f"{', '.join(f'{100 * old[i]:.0f}' for i in at)}%", end="")
steady_old = bool(np.all(np.diff(adult) >= tol))          # the decline moves steadily towards older ages
if rotates:
    print(f", most of the shift happening between e₀ = {lev[j_big]:g} and {lev[j_big + 1]:g}.  The rotation is "
          "therefore supported for the sources of gains in e₀; "
          + ("the age pattern of the decline itself moves the same way.\n" if steady_old else
             "the age pattern of the decline itself does not move steadily towards older ages.\n"))
else:
    print(".  These trajectories do not support a rotation of the sources of gains in e₀.\n")
```

## Step 7 — from a schedule back to its regime and e₀

Chapter 09 fits model schedules to data, which needs the inverse of the
generator (paper §5.1; the results below are in the companion only): the regime and e₀
whose generated schedule is closest to a
given schedule (`mdmx.trajectories.invert`: for each regime, a search over
e₀ for the smallest RMSE of logit($q_x$), then the best regime).  A random
sample of `{python} f"{PT['invert_sample']}"` observed country-years of the
non-noise regimes shows how well this recovers their regime and e₀.  It is
an in-sample check: the model and the regime labels were estimated from
these same schedules.

```{python}
#| label: c07-invert
#| code-summary: "Invert a sample of observed schedules (cached)"
def _invert():
    pool = np.flatnonzero(np.isin(labels, REGIMES))
    rng = np.random.default_rng(PT["invert_seed"])
    sample = np.sort(rng.choice(pool, size=min(PT["invert_sample"], pool.size), replace=False))
    rows = []
    for i in sample:
        found = tr.invert(z_obs[i], model, bracket=BRACKET, step=PT["invert_step"])
        rows.append({"row": int(i), "regime": int(labels[i]), "found": found["regime"],
                     "e0": float(e0[i]), "e0_found": found["e0"], "rmse": found["rmse"]})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


inv = artifacts.stage(
    "trajectories_inversion", _invert, inputs=["clustering", "tucker", "tensor", "trajectories"],
    params={"sample": PT["invert_sample"], "seed": PT["invert_seed"], "step": PT["invert_step"],
            "bracket": BRACKET, "regimes": REGIMES},
    code=[_invert, tr, clus, lifetable],
    desc="Regime and e0 recovered from a sample of observed schedules")
pool_all = np.isin(labels, REGIMES)
agree = float(np.mean(inv["found"] == inv["regime"]))
chance = float(np.max(np.bincount(labels[pool_all]) / pool_all.sum()))
e0_err = inv["e0_found"] - inv["e0"]
print(pd.crosstab(inv["regime"] + 1, inv["found"] + 1, rownames=["labelled"], colnames=["recovered"]))
print(f"\nRegime recovered for {100 * agree:.0f}% (largest regime's share: {100 * chance:.0f}%); "
      f"e0 error mean {e0_err.mean():+.2f}, mean absolute {e0_err.abs().mean():.2f} years")
latex.report("trajInvertAgree", 100 * agree, digits=0, desc="Percent of sampled schedules whose regime is recovered by inversion")
latex.report("trajInvertChance", 100 * chance, digits=0, desc="Share of the largest regime among non-noise country-years (percent)")
latex.report("trajInvertEzeroMae", float(e0_err.abs().mean()), digits=2,
             desc="Mean absolute difference between the e0 of the best-matching generated schedule and the schedule's own e0 (years)")
```

The regime is recovered for `{python} f"{100 * agree:.0f}"`% of the sampled
schedules, against `{python} f"{100 * chance:.0f}"`% for always guessing the
largest regime.  The regimes are summaries of a continuum of deviation
patterns (chapter 06), so a single schedule's regime can be ambiguous.
The e₀ of the best-matching generated schedule differs from the schedule's
own e₀ by `{python} f"{e0_err.abs().mean():.2f}"` years on average: the
closest schedule in logit($q_x$) is not always the one with the same life
expectancy.  Whether a fit should match the schedule or fix e₀ to the
data's is a question for chapter 09.

# The `trajectories` artefact

| Key | Shape / type | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `kind`, `candidate` | str | the chosen deviation (`lowess`, …) and its hold-out name |
| `e0_grid` | (g,) | e₀ grid (chapter 06) |
| `typical` | (g, r₁, r₂) | typical effective core on the grid |
| `deviation` | (K′, g, p) | each regime's deviation at its positions, on the grid (constant outside the support) |
| `support` | (K′, 2) | each regime's e₀ support |
| `clusters` | (K′,) int | the regimes served (chapter 06 labels; the noise cluster is not among them) |
| `feature_index` | (p, 2) | (sex component, age column) of each deviation entry: chapter 06's features plus the sex contrast of the level column if the chosen deviation uses it — *not* always `clustering["features"]["index"]` |
| `U_sex`, `U_age` | (S, r₁), (A, r₂) | the bases |
| `holdout_rmse` | DataFrame | pooled held-out RMSE of every candidate |

To generate the schedule of regime `k` at e₀ `x` (calibrated to `x`):

```python
logit_qx = tr.generate(art, k, x, bracket=P.section("trajectories")["calibration_bracket"])[0]   # (S, A)
```
